scope_notes: Static architecture review of the supplied snapshot; I did not run make verify, Go tests, browser journeys, or live provider calls.
Test files were read as evidence of intended interfaces and seams, not as proof that tests were executed or passed.
CSS and generated HTML assets were reviewed only for ownership/boundary structure, not visual design.
Runtime correctness of cancellation, transaction atomicity, concurrency, and supplier behavior is outside this static review.

checks.name: module_responsibilities
checks.reason: The declared relay module covers every internal/relay/*.go file, so identity, access, catalog, accounting, billing, routing, proxy, persistence and console HTTP are one Go package with no explicit capability interfaces. The package boundary is effectively a file-name boundary, not a module boundary.

findings.title: Backend capabilities are collapsed into one relay package and HTTP handlers own rule-rich SaaS logic
findings.principle: Modules own cohesive responsibilities; rule-rich SaaS capabilities need application/domain ownership with operation-level storage.
findings.impact: Identity, access, catalog, accounting, billing, routing, proxy and persistence share one Go package. Quota and billing changes are made in HTTP handlers with direct SQL, so module boundaries are not enforceable and unrelated capabilities are reviewed and tested together.
findings.recommendation: Extract rule-rich capabilities (identity/access, accounting/billing, routing) into packages with explicit application/domain and storage interfaces; keep console and proxy handlers as adapters; update architecture.json to enforce those boundaries.
findings.validation: Add dependency rules that forbid HTTP/SQL in domain packages and require HTTP handlers to call application interfaces; compile and run existing package and HTTP contract tests without behavior changes.

findings.title: Routing depends directly on net/http and database/sql and there is no upstream adapter boundary
findings.principle: Routing owns policy and runtime state without HTTP/SQL; upstream adapters own network/protocol and the gateway consumes explicit interfaces.
findings.impact: Routing policy cannot be reused or tested without HTTP requests and SQLite. Vendor protocol changes and storage changes touch the same policy package, and upstream substitution is not isolated behind an adapter.
findings.recommendation: Move routing selection, health and cooldown into a package with no net/http or database/sql imports; inject config/evidence storage interfaces; move outbound HTTP to an upstream adapter used by the gateway.
findings.validation: Add architecture rules forbidding net/http and database/sql in routing; verify routing policy tests run with fake config/evidence and HTTP adapter contract tests run separately.

findings.title: Server aggregates unrelated mutable state and one lock spans management and routing
findings.principle: Session, request, routing, health and business state have explicit owners; unrelated capabilities do not depend on one shared mutable object.
findings.impact: Session/auth state, routing runtimes, health/cooldown, latency pools, checking flags, config epoch and success evidence share one Server. Management and routing paths contend on the same lock, and lifecycle/cleanup ownership is unclear.
findings.recommendation: Split state owners (session store, routing runtime, health registry, console operation state) behind narrow interfaces; keep a composition root; use per-owner synchronization instead of one broad server lock.
findings.validation: Add concurrency tests that exercise management and dispatch concurrently and assert no shared-lock coupling; dependency rules prevent packages from reaching another owner's mutable state.

findings.title: Architecture declaration and project docs accept the central relay package despite target standards requiring separation
findings.principle: Project rules and executable declarations agree with target standards and do not waive requirements merely by describing current code.
findings.impact: The architecture check can be green while SaaS application/domain and gateway routing/upstream separation are absent. This gives false confidence and allows new responsibilities to keep accumulating in relay.
findings.recommendation: Either bring the implementation to the selected standards or record an explicit, reviewed exception with scope and follow-up gates; do not present the current declaration as satisfying the standards.
findings.validation: Compare architecture.json modules against the SaaS/gateway standards; add negative fixtures proving a handler with direct SQL or routing with net/http fails; review exception scope.

findings.title: Workspace console is one global script with page logic, state, API side effects and cleanup coupled
findings.principle: Features own business UI, interaction state, business API and cleanup; shared transport is business-neutral.
findings.impact: All pages share one mutable state object and one renderPage branch. Changes to billing, keys, models or records can affect unrelated pages; stale-request invalidation and cleanup are global, and feature-local API contracts are not enforced.
findings.recommendation: Split workspace.js into feature modules (billing, models, keys, tenants, records, playground) with local state/actions and cleanup; keep a thin shared transport and a composition entry.
findings.validation: Check that each feature can load and clean up independently, shared transport has no business/auth side effects beyond generic session expiry, and page modules expose narrow entry points.
